title: Automate KMS/TLS rotation for Private Installer using Vault, SealedSecrets, and optional HSM
author: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Adds automated KMS and TLS certificate rotation support for the Private Installer using HashiCorp Vault (transit + PKI), SealedSecrets re-encryption hooks, and optional HSM-backed KMS providers. Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private need automated, auditable rotation for TLS certs and KMS keys to meet compliance windows. This change unifies rotation across Terraform-managed cloud KMS, Vault-managed keys, and on-prem HSMs, and wires it into the Helm-based installer so upgrades can coordinate re-encryption and swap keys without downtime. What changed: 1) Terraform: new module redwood-private-installer/terraform/modules/kms that supports multiple backends (aws_kms, gcp_kms, hsm_via_pkcs11) and outputs a rotation_policy flag and key_identifiers. 2) Helm: added templates/rotation-cronjob.yaml and templates/post-upgrade-hook.yaml that deploy a rotation operator (lightweight cron controller) and a post-upgrade job to coordinate sealed-secrets rewrap. 3) Installer: private-installer-controller: new controller logic to detect rotation events from Vault and trigger staged rollouts: re-encrypt SealedSecrets, rotate TLS certs via cert-manager integrated with Vault, and gracefully roll pods to pick up new secrets. 4) Vault integration: new docs and sample manifests for enabling transit and PKI roles, and a bootstrap script to create policy + token for the installer. 5) SealedSecrets workflow: added a rewrap controller that can re-encrypt existing sealed secrets against a new public key and records migration status in annotations so rollbacks can detect in-flight rotations. 6) HSM support: expose PKCS#11 config hooks in TF module and installer to allow customers to plug in on-prem HSMs or cloud HSMs; rotation triggers call into HSM KMS plugin if present. 7) Upgrade/Rollback: installer upgrade hooks ensure a rotation in progress blocks automatic upgrade until staged rewrap completes or a manual override is given to prevent secret mismatch. Security and safety: rotations are performed in a staged, auditable manner with a dry-run mode for testing; Vault tokens scoped to least-privilege; telemetry emitted for each rotation phase; built-in rollback window where old keys are accepted until all workloads report new secret versions. Testing: unit tests for TF module, helm lint, integration e2e against a dev Vault and cert-manager in perf-canary, manual upgrade/rollback tests on simulated on-prem cluster. Migration: migration utility added under private-installer/scripts/rewrap.sh to migrate existing sealed-secrets to the new key, with idempotent behavior and progress checkpoints. Related: linked Linear tickets ENG-4821 (secrets rotation framework) and ENG-4940 (installer upgrade hooks). Checklist: - [x] Terraform module and examples - [x] Helm templates and operator - [x] SealedSecrets rewrap controller - [x] Vault docs and bootstrap scripts - [x] HSM plugin integration points - [x] Integration tests in perf-canary - [x] Docs/README and upgrade notes Rollout plan: feature gated behind installer flag enable_rotation=false by default; documented manual migration path; will enable by default in next minor release after soak.

upgrade_instructions: Before upgrading enable_rotation=false by default. To adopt rotation: 1) Bootstrap Vault PKI and transit roles with provided scripts and ensure installer token has the least-privileged policy per docs. 2) Run private-installer/scripts/rewrap.sh in dry-run mode to validate sealed-secret rewrap. 3) Set enable_rotation=true in values-private.yaml and apply Helm chart. 4) Monitor rotation_progress_count and rotation_duration_seconds metrics. 5) If issues, set enable_rotation=false and run rewrap.sh rollback mode to restore original sealed secrets. See redwood-docs/private/upgrade-rollback.md for full steps.
